newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Four East Timorese enter French embassy in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Four East Timorese enter French embassy in Jakarta.

text.p: Four East Timorese men broke into the French embassy in Jakarta before dawn on Tuesday to seek political asylum, witnesses said.

They said the four scaled the three-metre (nine-foot) high spiked iron fence surrounding the French embassy compound in central Jakarta, unfurling a banner while shouting "Viva East Timor" and other pro-independence slogans.
"We are seeking political asylum in France," one of the four men said.
"We are being chased by the Indonesian armed forces for taking part in a demonstration in (the East Timor capital) Dili in November," another asylum seeker said.
The demonstration took place on November 25 outside the offices of Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo after he gave a news conference attended by both local and foreign media.
Two of the four men, aged between 18 and 26, said they were high school students while the other two said they were students at the University of East Timor in Dili.

The men were met by two embassy officials in plain clothes and body searched before being taken inside a building within the compound. One Indonesian soldier and a policeman watched from outside the compound fence.

Since September 1995, 96 young East Timorese who have broken into foreign embassies in Jakarta have been given asylum in Portugal, the former colonial power in the enclave invaded by Indonesia in December 1975.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the administering power in the territory.
The men said they did not want asylum in Portugal.
"There are already many of our brothers in Portugal. We want to go to France," one of the men said.

In the last such asylum bid in December, three Timorese who entered the French embassy left for asylum in Portugal around 12 hours after entering the compound. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) helped organise their travel.
East Timorese sources said these three were also involved in the November 25 protest.
It is has been the Indonesian government's policy to allow such asylum seekers to leave unhindered.
Indonesian police in East Timor have already arrested at least three youths for their involvement in the protest.
Police had threatened those involved with up to 20 years in prison for spreading hatred against President Suharto after a banner was displayed reading in part: "Suharto eats East Timorese bones".
